title: Understanding Stragglers in Large Model Training Using What-if Analysis
problem: Stragglers (slow workers) significantly impact distributed large model training performance, but identifying root causes requires complex analysis
motivation: Distributed training for large LLMs is expensive; understanding and eliminating stragglers is critical for training efficiency
method: When training large AI models across multiple computers, the slowest worker (a straggler) forces everyone to wait, significantly slowing the entire system. This work uses what-if analysis—testing different parameter scenarios like batch size, network bandwidth, or hardware configuration to predict their effects—to understand which workers will become stragglers and why. By simulating these scenarios in advance, you can identify the root causes of slowdowns (like insufficient network bandwidth or imbalanced computation) and make better decisions about how to distribute the training work.
key_novelty: What-if analysis can predict which workers will slow down distributed model training and identify the root causes of those slowdowns.
contributions: What-if analysis framework for straggler diagnosis
limitations: Title-only paper; specific metrics and results unknown; applicability to different training scenarios unclear
